title: fix: type image path when pasting clipboard images into terminals
head: 0f8191ec10b3
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Omarchy-tagged TUI terminal classes are omitted from image path routing
leads.consequence: The stock terminal tag recognizes org.omarchy.* and TUI.*; org.omarchy.btop, org.omarchy.bash, and TUI.float have no substring recognized by the new predicate. Selecting an image there still sends Shift+Insert with image/png, contrary to the new behavior, even though the Super+V shortcut treats these as terminals. Conversely arbitrary GUI classes containing 'foot' or 'term' receive a typed file path rather than an image paste.

leads.summary: An image path containing a newline injects Return into the recipient
leads.consequence: Both HOME/XDG_STATE_HOME and user-editable history path strings can contain a newline. wtype 0.4 maps a newline character to the Return key. Thus choosing that image from history presses Return partway through the path in the foreground terminal, potentially executing a partially typed shell line or prematurely submitting an agent prompt. Spaces, quote marks, and shell metacharacters are also sent raw, so even an ordinary home path with whitespace is not a usable single shell filename token. The script suppresses wtype errors and exits success, with image/png left on the clipboard.
leads.triage: dropped; requires a newline in HOME/XDG_STATE_HOME or hand-edited history JSON; stored names are <sha256>.<ext>. Spaces point already covered by Opus F3 (not published).

leads.summary: Relative image paths beginning with a dash are parsed by wtype as flags
leads.consequence: The public helper accepts a readable relative file (for example -image.png) and publishes its contents, but `wtype "$path"` invokes wtype 0.4's option parser. A dash-prefixed final argument fails with 'Missing argument to -image.png' instead of typing anything; stderr is discarded, `|| true` makes the branch exit successfully and Shift+Insert is not tried. Use `wtype -- "$path"` (or normalize to an absolute path) and cover this input in the test.

leads.summary: Origin-focus PRs #12991 and #13103 conflict with the path branch and require classification after refocus
leads.consequence: Both open PRs separately pass the clipboard overlay's origin window to the helper and refocus it before sending the paste key. Neither is stacked with this PR. Merging the script as-is with either PR yields conflict markers in the paste block, despite each other PR currently reporting MERGEABLE against quattro; their test files conflict too. If resolved by keeping the new early path branch, it types into whichever window Hyprland focused after the overlay closes, bypassing the origin refocus on image selections. If resolved by keeping only their branch, path typing disappears. Refocus first, then classify the verified recipient before typing.

leads.summary: Open PR #10536's native-image Ctrl+V path is overridden for every recognized terminal
leads.consequence: #10536 changes the final chord to Ctrl+V specifically to pass image paste through the terminal to image-aware apps, while this PR exits before that chord for every recognized terminal and instead types a path. Its own new fixture requires Ctrl+V for a normal image selection. The script merges textually, but the test file has a conflict hunk and the two features' terminal results cannot both hold without selecting behavior explicitly (for example an opt-in path action). The other PR is currently MERGEABLE against quattro, and its head diverges from this one.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F6; Opus self-check confirmed test contradiction

leads.summary: The new fixture cannot detect a predicate that works for foot alone
leads.consequence: The only positive image/terminal case is class=foot. A plausible broken implementation `[[ $class == foot ]]` passes all four new assertions: Firefox and empty class still use Shift+Insert, and text/plain still bypasses classification. It misses the other three supported terminal defaults and the custom Omarchy app-IDs. Add positive cases for the class IDs from default/hypr/apps/terminals.lua and a negative GUI class containing a matching substring, and assert the hyprctl arguments in the stub.
leads.triage: confirmed (coordinator read of the four assertions; Opus self-check run 49ac5ed3 P1 77/77)

leads.summary: The manual's categorical claim about image-capable terminal applications contradicts its own Ctrl+V guidance
leads.consequence: The new sentence says terminals can only receive text, without distinguishing a terminal emulator's paste-text action from a program receiving Ctrl+V and reading image data from the clipboard. The same page already instructs users to use Ctrl+V in agent harnesses for images. Stock Foot maps Shift+Insert to its own clipboard-text paste but leaves Ctrl+V to its child (unless user overrides the binding). This can mislead users into choosing path typing rather than native image input for agents that support it. Qualify the statement to distinguish Shift+Insert from Ctrl+V.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** picking an image from clipboard history with Return while a stock foot, Alacritty, kitty or Ghostty window is focused classifies that terminal correctly and types the stored image's absolute path. Hyprland keeps reporting the origin window through `hyprctl activewindow` while the picker holds keyboard focus. `--copy-only` still sends no keystroke, and non-image files, other GUI windows and undetectable focus (`{}`, empty class, failing `hyprctl`) keep Shift+Insert. The four new tests pass on this head and on a local merge with current `quattro`, and the terminal case fails against the base script.

The main suggestion is to reuse Omarchy's existing `terminal` tag instead of a new class list. That tag also covers Omarchy's own agent window.

### Terminal detection diverges from the `terminal` tag and misses `org.omarchy.agent`

Omarchy already defines what counts as a terminal in `default/hypr/apps/terminals.lua`, which tags `(Alacritty|kitty|com.mitchellh.ghostty|foot|org\.codeberg\.dnkl\.foot|wezterm|org\.omarchy\..*|TUI\..*)` as `+terminal`. `default/hypr/bindings/clipboard.lua` uses that tag for `Super + C` / `Super + V` "so there's one definition of what counts as a terminal". The new `terminal_focused` uses a separate substring list, and the two disagree:

```text
window class                       terminal tag   this PR
org.omarchy.agent                  yes            Shift+Insert (nothing pasted)
org.omarchy.btop, TUI.float        yes            Shift+Insert
xterm, org.kde.konsole, footclient no             types path
io.gitlab.adhami3310.Footage (GUI) no             types path   ("foot" substring)
foot, Alacritty, kitty,            yes            types path   (both agree)
com.mitchellh.ghostty
```

The table comes from sandboxed runs of the head script with a stubbed `hyprctl` that returns each class and its tags.

**Impact:** `omarchy agent` (`Super + Shift + Ctrl + A`) and the scratchpad console launch agents with `--app-id=org.omarchy.agent` (`bin/omarchy-agent`). In those windows, picking an image still pastes nothing, although this is the agent-harness case the new manual sentence describes. Non-terminal apps whose class contains `term` or `foot` get a typed path instead of the usual Shift+Insert paste.

**Suggested change:** read the tag from `hyprctl activewindow -j`. Hyprland reports window-rule tags there with a trailing `*`:

```bash
terminal_focused() {
  hyprctl activewindow -j 2>/dev/null |
    jq -e '(.tags // []) | any(. == "terminal" or . == "terminal*")' >/dev/null 2>&1
}
```

In the same sandbox this types the path for exactly the tagged classes. The test's `hyprctl` stub would need to emit `tags` as well as `class`. If xterm, Konsole or Tilix should count as terminals, extending the tag in `terminals.lua` would cover `Super + C` / `Super + V` for them too.

### The window is classified before the 150 ms delay

`terminal_focused` runs in the `if` condition, then `sleep 0.15`, then `wtype`.

**Impact:** after a mouse pick, Hyprland's focus-follows-mouse can move focus to the window under the pointer once the picker closes (the event sequence in #12987 shows this). The check can then see the origin terminal while the path is typed into another window, or the reverse. Keyboard picks are normally not affected (#12987 reports that they paste correctly).

**Suggested change:** sleep first, then classify the window that will receive the keys. With that order the PR's tests still pass. If #12991 or #13103 (origin-window refocus) lands, the check belongs after that refocus. Both currently conflict textually with this PR in `bin/omarchy-clipboard-paste-file`.

### Additional notes

**Suggested change (small):** use `wtype -- "$path"`. wtype 0.4 parses any argument starting with `-` as an option, so a relative path such as `-shot.png` passed through the CLI types nothing, and `2>/dev/null || true` hides the error. Paths from the history picker are absolute, so this only affects direct CLI use. The test's expected `wtype` arguments change with it.

**Documentation:** the new manual sentence follows "ready to paste on `Super + V`", but `Super + V` never types a path. Only picking an image in the history picker does. The page's own note (line 14) says most agent harnesses use `Ctrl + V` for pasting images, so "terminals can only receive text" is too broad: the terminal's paste action is text-only, while programs inside it can read images from the clipboard. The script comment makes the same claim. A possible rewording: "Picking an image in clipboard history while a terminal is focused types its file path instead, since the terminal's own paste only handles text." Mentioning `Shift + Return` (copy only, no typed path) would help harness users who prefer `Ctrl + V`.

**Optional test improvement:** `foot` is the only positive terminal case, so a predicate of `[[ $class == foot ]]` passes all four new assertions (confirmed with a mutated script in the sandbox). Cases for `org.omarchy.agent` and a GUI class containing `foot` or `term` would pin the detection above.

**Related work:** issue #10526 reports this problem and is not referenced. #10536 (send Ctrl+V so image-aware terminal programs read the image), #13070 and #7422 take different approaches to it. #10536's test expects Ctrl+V for the same image paste, so the two cannot both hold as written. The first Verification bullet in the PR description (commandcode, qwenaudio, colibri) appears to belong to #11839.

---
